title: Reading with care
hookLine: reading tafsir with teachers and humility
tomorrow: what if your day already had a frame built in?

lines: THE BOOKS ARE ON THE SHELF.
cards: You can watch every video there is on fixing a leaky sink and still end up calling your uncle, who comes over, looks once, and says: not that part, this one. Books are like that too.

You've got the commentaries now: al-Tabari's voices, Ibn Kathir's order, al-Qurtubi's rulings, al-Mizan's balance, the Jalals' doorway. So who do you ask? The tradition's answer is old and plain: a teacher.

teach.b: The Qur'an tells people who don't know to ask those who do. And it tells a story about it.
Moses, a prophet who spoke with God, meets a man of knowledge, whom tradition calls al-Khidr, and asks: may I follow you, so you can teach me? Even Moses asks.

teach.h: FACE TO FACE, A CHAIN OF TEACHERS.
teach.b: Reciters of the Qur'an still learn it face to face, and a teacher can grant an ijaza, a license naming the chain of teachers behind it. The prayer the Qur'an gives for this is short: "My Lord! Increase me in knowledge."
Reading with care means the book, a commentary, and a person who can say: not that part, this one.
Now, the commentators, back in one breath. Al-Tabari: all the voices. Ibn Kathir: the book explains itself.
Al-Qurtubi: law in the verses. Tabataba'i: the balance. The two Jalals: short and clear.

how: Muslims learning tafsir usually read it in a circle or class with a teacher; Qur'an reciters learn face to face and may receive an ijaza naming their chain of teachers.

o: reading only translations, never the original Arabic
reading as fast as possible to finish the whole book
reading scripture with a teacher, and the humility to ask

games.q: a verse screenshot is going around with no context, and it sounds harsh. a friend asks you what it means. what does reading with care look like?
o: share it on; the words speak for themselves.
read the verses around it, a commentary, then ask a teacher.

games.why: the context, a commentary, and a person who knows: the book, the notes, the teacher.

practice: Close your eyes and bring back one teacher who once helped you understand something, a parent, a coach, someone at school or the mosque. Remember the moment it clicked.
Then let one question form, about a verse or any line you've wondered about, that you'd bring to someone like them.

wordCard.voice: Reading with care: reading the Qur'an and its commentaries with a teacher, and with the humility to ask.

carryVoice: Last line of reading the sources: with a teacher, the way even Moses asked. The whole stretch, read and done.
